card.name: The letter g inside split-up words
card.fires_on: A bare g or G (sometimes with a hyphen or space) that starts the second part of a word the text has split, such as city-g|arden, temple g|ables or G|ospels. It also fires on other word-internal pieces like log or progn.

modes.label: g after a compound start
modes.description: A lone g begins the second half of a compound or split noun, often after a noun like city, temple or steel.
modes.example: with its temple<< g>>ables and classic columns

modes.label: g at the start of Gospel
modes.description: A lone g or G begins the word Gospel(s) or a similar g-word.
modes.example: the<< G>>ospels were written by an enlightened being

modes.label: Other mid-word pieces
modes.description: A piece in the middle of a long, rare word, where the next piece completes it.

card.writes: It promotes odd word pieces and non-English characters, so it adds no clear meaning.
card.plain: It fires when a word is cut up and a lone g starts the next piece, as in garden, gables or Gospels.
